chunks: And it was narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man travels for trade to Mecca, or he has camels which he rents out. Is his Hajj considered incomplete or complete?' He said: 'No, rather his Hajj is complete.'
ai.seo_question: Does traveling for trade or renting camels invalidate a man's obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that delegating the physical performance of Hajj rituals to a proxy does not diminish the validity of the obligatorily incumbent Hajj (Hajj al-Islam), provided the individual fulfills the core requirements. This ruling addresses the practical concerns of merchants and those with livestock, affirming that the spiritual and legal completeness of the Hajj remains intact even when the pilgrim is not physically present for every ritual act. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the sufficiency of the proxy's action for the principal's obligation.
